To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
graphene on hBN can be a potential candidate for graphene-based electronics, and that graphone on hBN can have a large band gap of more than 2.4 eV.
the band gaps of graphene and graphene on hexagonal born nitride (h-BN) are on the order of tens of meV and 2.5 to 3 eV respectively.
the band gap in graphene supported on hB N is small (about 0.1eV) and is vulnerable to misalignment, while graphone supported on hBN has large band gap (>2.5eV) and it is robust against misalignment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic properties of graphene and graphon on a hexagonal boron-nitride (hBN), which has recently emerged as a promising candidate for the graphene substrate material.
the electronic structure and band gap engineering of two-dimensional graphene based materials, namely graphene and hydrogenated graphene (graphone).
the study of the electronic properties of the graphene on hBN and graphone on hBN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the graphene/hBN interface is not suitable for band gap opening, whereas graphone/hBN system is an excellent system to achieve a band gap of 2.5-3.0 eV.
graphene on hBN is a good substrate for graphene based devices, but graphone on hBN is even better.
graphene supported on hB N is not a good choice as a channel material in field effect transistor applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graphene on hBN can provide a platform for band gap opening in a controlled manner.
the band gap engineering of graphone is possible by controlling the hydrogenation and the substrate material, and that the band gap of graphene/hBN system is vulnerable to slight misalignment.
graphene on hBN is a promising system to study the fundamental physics of graphene, and graphone on hBN could be a viable candidate for graphene based post-silicon electronic devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
graphene on hBN can have a finite band gap if graphene is aligned with hBN, and the band gap can be significantly enhanced by hydrogenating graphene.
the band gap of graphene can be engineered to a desired value by chemical functionalization and the substrate material can be used as dielectric in the devices.
graphene/hBN is a promising system for graphene based nanostructures and that graphone is an attractive channel material for graphene based field effect transistors.
